analysis:
Examined all supplied metadata, patches and source against the canonical definition index and selected details. This batch changes tests only; no concrete production security regression is established, and assertions are not proof that implementations enforce their contracts.
AddonIPCServerTests.swift:88-170 exercises private socket/directory modes, framing, oversized-message closure, unauthenticated-peer rejection before dispatch, stale/live socket handling and stop cleanup. The injected permissive authenticator at :78 is test-only. AddonIPCTests.swift:19-98 tests bounded leases, malformed inputs, 8-KiB messages and limited response fields; :104-146 tests hold priority over update/reconnect and preservation of lifecycle/model-switch drains. AutopilotBusyReasonTests.swift head patch :17,218-220,247-249 adds hold reporting and test-state cleanup without changing production authorization.
ProviderBusyWireTests.swift:37-95 covers optional busy metadata in registration/heartbeat, raw-attestation encoding, unknown-reason decoding and omission alongside routable heartbeat status. These introduce no demonstrated prompt/key/token exposure or billing change. T-041 cache crypto/scoping is not modified in the supplied files.
Integration must examine the actual AddonIPCServer, AddonPeerPolicy, hold manager, ProviderDrain and CoordinatorClient changes: bind signed peer identity to addon/hold ownership (TB-003), bound connection resources, handle filesystem races, expire leases reliably, and preserve update/reconnect/shutdown behavior. Verify hold release cannot restore serving with stale authorization (TB-002, TB-011, T-053), that attestation control remains responsive (T-057), and that draining registration/routing is enforced rather than inferred from the test comment. Those implementations and coordinator behavior are outside this batch, so these remain material unverified contracts, not findings.
